text.p: Electronics group Singatronics Ltd said in a statement on Thursday it has closed its Singapore manufacturing arm and its programme management arm in the U.S., effective today.
The Singapore operation had been loss-making for the last few years and the directors did not believe that it could turn around in the forseeable future, the company said.
The closure of the Singapore operation will result in the redundancy of the employees. The statement did not say how many employees were affected and company officials were unavailable for comment.

The impact of the closures is expected to be a one-time loss of Singapore $5 million. "The continuous operating loss previously incurred by the Singapore manufacturing operation will however, cease immediately," the company added.
It said it would concentrate its contract manufacturing business at its Malaysia subsidiary, which has been performing profitably.
The company said it believes that with the these moves it should return to profitability in 1997. In September, it reported a pre-tax loss of S$1.69 million for the first half.
